WOODWORK — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Design in Woodwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Design in Woodwork.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Design in Woodwork.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Design in Woodwork.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Design in Woodwork.

2. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Input Cable Tester

3. When learning Furniture Making, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Furniture Making.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Furniture Making.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Furniture Making.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Furniture Making.

4. When learning Blending wood with other materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Blending wood with other materials.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Blending wood with other materials.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Blending wood with other materials.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Blending wood with other materials.

5. When learning Project Activity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Project Activity.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project Activity.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project Activity.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project Activity.

6. When learning Upholstery, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Upholstery.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Upholstery.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Upholstery.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Upholstery.

7. When learning Framed Wooden Doors and Windows, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.

8. When learning Emergency Management, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Emergency Management.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Emergency Management.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Emergency Management.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Emergency Management.

9. When learning Estimation of Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Estimation of Materials.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Estimation of Materials.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Estimation of Materials.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Estimation of Materials.

10. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Ignore burnt cables

11. When learning Fittings, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Fittings.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Fittings.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Fittings.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Fittings.

12. When learning Occupational Information, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Occupational Information.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Occupational Information.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Occupational Information.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Occupational Information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Furniture Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Framed Wooden Doors and Windows and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Fittings and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Upholstery and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. A — Information and Communication Technology

3. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Furniture Making.

4. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Blending wood with other materials.

5. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project Activity.

6. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Upholstery.

7. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.

8. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Emergency Management.

9. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Estimation of Materials.

10. B — Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Fittings.

12. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Occupational Information.
